$comment: Blocks retired from public/content/ under hard rule 1a of the visual compaction brief, and the
figure that took over each one's job.
RULE 1a, IN FULL: an ASCII or box-drawing diagram, a pseudo-table inside a code block, a stack
of near-identical cards or a restated 'summary' table may be deleted ONCE a figure renders the
same facts. A visual takes over the job only when it shows every fact, number, tier label and
source the text it replaces carried — and every figure keeps a 'View the data' disclosure
generated from its data file, so the numbers stay on the page and stay in the printed PDF.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. scripts/verify-content-integrity.mjs compares every body line against the
baseline and fails the build on anything that moved, which is exactly right: the restructure
moved body text, it did not rewrite it. A retirement is the one thing this brief authorises
that the guard cannot tell apart from a quiet deletion. Declaring it costs one entry and a
sentence saying which figure carries the facts — the same bargain notation-rewrites.json
strikes for prose, and scripts/figure-migrations.json for figures leaving the markdown.
`facts` is not decoration. It is the checklist the figure is held to, and Phase 8's report
itemises the words retired against it. If a fact listed here is not visible in the figure or in
its 'View the data' table, the retirement is not authorised and the block goes back.
